reason: This passage (Numbers 22-24) depicts Yahweh actively protecting and blessing Israel through the prophet Balaam. When Yahweh speaks in this text, He prevents Balaam from cursing Israel and instead puts blessings in Balaam's mouth. The prophetic utterances declare Israel's future greatness, prosperity, and divine favor ('How goodly are thy tents, O Jacob...'). The complaints about Israel's presence and power come from Balak of Moab and the Moabites, not from Yahweh. Yahweh's role is one of affirmation and protection of the people, not complaint.
